nodes.title: Edit Guardrails
widgets_values: Keep every other part of the photograph exactly as it is. The drawn lines are only a guide to where the subject goes, how big it is and what pose it holds: erase them completely, leaving none of the drawn marks, colour or outline anywhere in the result. Render the subject as a real part of the scene, matching the photograph’s own lighting direction, colour temperature, contrast and grain, and ground it with contact shading where it meets the surface. If the scene’s own light casts shadows, give it a cast shadow that matches them in direction, length and softness; if the light is overhead or comes from behind the camera, keep the shadow small and directly beneath it, and if the light comes from behind the subject, let its edges catch that light instead of casting a shadow toward the camera. Do not add glow, haze, or an outline of light around it. Let nearby foreground elements overlap its edges.
